title: Design a Distributed Rate Limiter
subtitle: From single-node Token Bucket middleware to multi-region Redis sliding logs

stages.title: Stage 1 — Local In-Memory Token Bucket
stages.bottleneck: Memory limits on single app server & inability to share state across multiple API servers.
stages.narrative:
**In-memory token bucket middleware.** Each incoming API request checks a local hash map on the app server. If tokens exist for the API key, decrement count and forward request to DB. Otherwise, return `429 Too Many Requests`.

**Limitation:** When app servers scale horizontally, a user hitting Server A doesn't update token counts on Server B.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Centralized Redis Counter
stages.bottleneck: Race conditions under heavy parallel traffic (two concurrent requests reading & writing token count at once).
stages.narrative:
**Centralized state in Redis.** All app servers talk to Redis for rate-limiting using fixed window counters (`user_id:minute`).

**Atomic Operations:** Lua scripts or `INCR` + `EXPIRE` ensure atomic reads and writes, eliminating local state skew across app servers.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Sliding Window Log in Redis Cluster
stages.bottleneck: Traffic spikes at window boundaries (e.g. 100 requests at 1:00:59 and 100 requests at 1:01:01).
stages.narrative: **Sliding Window Log with Redis Sorted Sets (ZSET).** Store timestamps of every request as scores in a ZSET. Remove elements older than `now - 60s`, count remaining items. Smooths out boundary spikes completely.

stages.title: Stage 4 — Global Distributed Edge Rate Limiting
stages.bottleneck: Cross-region network latency to a central Redis cluster slowing down global API responses.
stages.narrative: **Edge rate limiting.** Requests are evaluated directly at 300+ CDN edge locations worldwide. Rejected requests never reach origin servers, cutting infrastructure costs and protecting backends from DDoS.
